name: Freshchat
tagline: The widest native channel list you can buy for $19 an agent — with the actual AI unbundled and billed by the session.
tldr: Freshchat is Freshworks' customer messaging product: a web/mobile chat widget plus WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS, LINE, Apple Business Chat, Google Business Messages, and email feeding one agent inbox. It's sold standalone and also bundled into Freshdesk Omni (the product formerly marketed as Freshworks Customer Service Suite).
Pricing is straightforward per-agent SaaS: Free for up to 10 agents, then Growth $19, Pro $49, Enterprise $79 per agent/month billed annually — with monthly rates not published on the pricing page.

The differentiator is channel breadth at the entry price. Nine-plus native channels on a $19 plan is more than most competitors give you at three times the cost, and the free tier is genuinely usable at up to 10 agents rather than 2.

Real strength: the unified inbox and setup experience. G2 (~4.4/5 across roughly 490 reviews) and Capterra (4.2/5 across 151 reviews) reviewers consistently single out the single-interface, multi-channel view and the low learning curve.

Real weakness: the AI is a separately-metered add-on, not a feature. Freddy AI Agent is $49 per 100 sessions on top of your seat cost, and multiple Capterra reviewers describe the built-in AI and reporting as thin — one flatly says advanced capabilities and AI features are "pretty much missing."

Best for teams already inside the Freshworks stack, or channel-heavy support orgs (WhatsApp, Instagram, SMS) that want breadth cheaply and are willing to treat AI automation as a line item they turn on later.
keyFeatures: Unified agent inbox where every connected channel (web, mobile SDK, WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS, LINE, email) lands in one workspace
Freddy AI Agent — an add-on conversational agent that answers from your knowledge base and takes real actions (order tracking, exchanges, inventory checks, plan changes) through connected systems
Freddy AI Copilot for agents ($29/agent/month, annual) with reply assistance and Live Translate
Assignment rules that auto-route conversations on message text, source, priority, skill, user and account properties; intelligent routing on Pro, skill-based routing on Enterprise
Private notes with @mentions to pull teammates into a conversation, plus manual assignment to agents or groups
Canned responses that can be categorised, kept private, or shared and assigned across teams and groups
Live Translate — auto-detects the customer's browser language and translates agent replies in real time
REST API v2 (conversations, messages, users, agents, groups, roles, reports) plus webhooks and the Freshworks developer platform/marketplace

companyInfo.founded: Freshchat launched September 2017; parent company Freshworks Inc. founded 2010
companyInfo.funding: Publicly traded — Freshworks Inc. trades on NASDAQ as FRSH; Freshchat is a product line, not separately funded
companyInfo.employees: ~5,300 across Freshworks Inc. (2025 reporting); Freshchat-specific headcount is not disclosed

faq.question: Is Freshchat still a product, or was it folded into Freshworks Customer Service Suite?
faq.answer: Both. Freshchat is still sold and priced standalone at freshworks.com/live-chat-software with its own Free/Growth/Pro/Enterprise tiers. Separately, Freshworks bundles Freshchat with Freshdesk ticketing and voice into a suite that was marketed as Customer Service Suite and has since been renamed Freshdesk Omni. If you only want messaging, you can still buy just Freshchat.

faq.question: What does Freshchat actually cost?
faq.answer: Free for up to 10 agents, then $19/agent/month (Growth), $49 (Pro), and $79 (Enterprise), all billed annually. Freshworks does not publish monthly-billing rates on the Freshchat pricing page, so assume they're higher. AI is priced separately: Freddy AI Agent at $49 per 100 sessions and Freddy AI Copilot at $29/agent/month.

faq.question: Is the AI included in the plan price?
faq.answer: No. Freshworks gives paid plans 500 free Freddy AI Agent sessions once per account, and after that it's $49 per 100 sessions on top of seat costs. That's the single biggest thing to model before comparing Freshchat's $19 headline to competitors that bundle AI conversations into the tier price.

faq.question: Does Freshchat handle phone calls?
faq.answer: Not natively. Freshchat is a messaging product — chat, social, SMS, and email. Voice comes from Freshdesk Contact Center, a separate Freshworks product bundled into Freshdesk Omni. If phone is a requirement, you're buying the suite, not Freshchat.

faq.question: How good is Freshchat's reporting?
faq.answer: Adequate rather than deep, and tier-dependent. There's a chat conversations overview covering volume, performance, and CSAT trends, custom dashboards from Pro up, and a Freddy AI Agent report with a ticket deflection rate. But Capterra reviewers repeatedly flag "no advanced reporting" as a weakness, so treat analytics as a reason to check the trial carefully rather than a selling point.

faq.question: Why is Freshchat's Trustpilot score so low compared to G2 and Capterra?
faq.answer: Freshchat.com's Trustpilot page sits at 1.9/5 — but on only 12 reviews, which is far too small a sample to weigh against G2's ~490 or Capterra's 151. What's more useful is that the themes there (broken push notifications, unhelpful support) match complaints that also appear in Capterra reviews, so they're corroborated even if the score itself isn't statistically meaningful.

criteriaScores.note: Freshworks' own messaging-channels page and the Freshchat pricing tiers list web chat, mobile in-app SDK, email, WhatsApp Business, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, SMS, LINE, Apple Business Chat, and Google Business Messages — one of the broadest native lists in this price band. Telephone voice is the gap: that's Freshdesk Contact Center, a separate product (freshworks.com/customer-service-suite/features/messaging-channels/, freshworks.com/live-chat-software/pricing/).

Freshworks documents one inbox with conversations continuing across channels without losing context, and Capterra reviewers independently confirm the experience — Vaishnava S. calls out that "it brings conversations from multiple channels into a single interface." Docked one point because social channels sit behind the $19 Growth tier, so the Free plan isn't actually omnichannel.

Freddy AI Agent is a genuine agent, not smart-replies: Freshworks documents it taking real-time actions like tracking orders, processing exchanges, checking inventory, and changing subscriptions via connected systems. The point off is structural — it's a metered add-on ($49/100 sessions), not part of the product you're buying (freshworks.com/freshdesk/omni/freddy-ai-agent/).

Freshworks' only public accuracy figure I could find is a customer case study (Hobbycraft, 82% first-contact resolution) — vendor-published and unaudited. Independent Capterra reviewers pull the other way: Santhosh S. writes "there aren't many advanced capabilities, and AI features are pretty much missing," and Akshith N. that "AI features are limited." No independent benchmark exists, so this score follows the review sentiment, not the case study.

Freddy AI Agent learns from knowledge base articles as its primary source and can additionally ingest URLs and training materials automatically — Freshworks docs note it can take up to 30 minutes to learn from a URL. No manual intent-building required (crmsupport.freshworks.com knowledge-sources articles).

Freshworks documents grounding answers in a verified knowledge base plus "prompt shields" to block out-of-context prompts, and its own Freddy guidance warns that missing conditions in source articles can cause hallucinations — honest, but it puts the burden on your content. I could not verify per-answer source citation shown to the end customer, which is why this isn't a 4.

Assignment rules fire on message text, source, priority, skill, and app/user/account properties, with intelligent routing on Pro and skill-based routing on Enterprise; separately, Freddy AI Agent chains multi-step actions across Shopify, Stripe, PayPal, and FedEx rather than answering and stopping (crmsupport.freshworks.com assignment-rules docs, freshworks.com/freshdesk/omni/freddy-ai-agent/).

Freshworks does ship Freddy sentiment analysis for real-time ticket sentiment and prioritisation — but the documentation for it lives under Freshdesk, and it does not appear in Freshchat's own published plan feature lists. Scored low deliberately: if you buy Freshchat standalone, I could not verify you get it (support.freshdesk.com sentiment-analysis article).

The shared inbox is the product's centre of gravity and its most consistently praised element across both G2 (~4.4/5, ~490 reviews) and Capterra (4.2/5, 151 reviews), where reviewers specifically credit the single-interface multi-channel view. Not a 5 because the deepest ticketing and cross-team workflow lives in Freshdesk, not Freshchat.

Freshworks states AI agents "know exactly when (and how) to escalate" and "transfer conversations with full context," and Freshchat's own assignment rules and manual assign-to-agent-or-group actions handle the human side of the handoff (freshworks.com/freshdesk/omni/freddy-ai-agent/, crmsupport.freshworks.com inbox-actions docs).

Private notes give context to another agent on handoff, @mention tags a teammate inside a note and notifies them immediately, and conversations can be assigned manually or by rule to an agent or group. Freshchat agents can also spin an internal task into a Freshdesk ticket for back-office SMEs (crmsupport.freshworks.com responding/assignment articles).

Canned responses can be categorised, kept in a private category, or shared and assigned across the team, with group-level canned responses added in a documented Freshchat release (community.freshworks.com Freshchat release notes).

Shopify is one of six integrations Freshworks features by name on the Freshchat integrations page, and Freddy AI Agent's documented action list includes tracking orders and shipping status through connected commerce systems including Shopify — real data access, not just a contact sync (freshworks.com/live-chat-software/integrations/, freshworks.com/freshdesk/omni/freddy-ai-agent/).

There is no first-party Freshworks WooCommerce integration for Freshchat that I could find. The marketplace listing is a third-party app ("WooCommerce by ChargeDesk"), which means support and roadmap sit outside Freshworks (freshworks.com/apps/freshchat/woocommerce_by_chargedesk).

An official Freshchat plugin is listed in the WordPress.org plugin directory and installable from the WP admin, and Freshchat's admin has a dedicated Admin > Integrations > WordPress screen that hands you the widget code — a real first-party path, not a copy-paste workaround (wordpress.org/support/plugin/freshchat/, crmsupport.freshworks.com WordPress integration article).

I found no Freshchat app in the Wix App Market. Installation is manual embedding of the widget snippet through Wix's custom-code feature, which itself requires a Wix Premium plan — and the Wix Studio community forum thread on embedding the Freshchat widget suggests it isn't frictionless (forum.wixstudio.com "EMBED FRESHCHAT WIDGET CODE ON WIX WEBSITE").

No dedicated app. Freshworks' own install docs tell you to paste the snippet into Squarespace's Advanced > Code Injection header — functional, but manual, and it breaks if Squarespace changes code injection (crmsupport.freshworks.com chat-widget install article).

No native Webflow app or listing found. Freshworks' documented route is pasting the script into Webflow's Project Settings > Custom Code footer — the same generic snippet path as any other site (crmsupport.freshworks.com chat-widget install article).

Make.com publishes a Freshchat integration, and Freshworks' marketplace carries 1,000+ apps. But Zapier's own community answers that there is no dedicated Freshchat Zapier app — the official Zapier connectors are for Freshdesk and Freshsales Suite, so Freshchat users route through those or through webhooks. n8n support for Freshchat specifically I could not verify (make.com/en/integrations/freshchat, community.zapier.com thread on Freshchat/Freshdesk).

Salesforce is a named featured integration on the Freshchat integrations page, and Freshsales (Freshworks' own CRM) is natively adjacent. HubSpot and Pipedrive I could not verify as first-party Freshchat integrations — they may exist in the 1,000+ marketplace, but Freshworks doesn't surface them for this product (freshworks.com/live-chat-software/integrations/).

Freshworks explicitly documents Freddy AI Agent tracking orders and shipping status, checking inventory availability, processing exchanges and scheduling pickups, and retrieving flight updates via integrations with Shopify, Stripe, PayPal, and FedEx — the bot reads live system state rather than describing it. Caveat: this is the paid AI add-on, not the base seat (freshworks.com/freshdesk/omni/freddy-ai-agent/).

Live Translate auto-detects the customer's language from browser settings and translates agent replies in real time, and Topics/FAQ articles can be translated per configured language; Freddy Copilot adds its own Live Translate for agents. One catch worth knowing: Freshchat's own Live Translate setup doc requires you to supply a Google Translate API key (crmsupport.freshworks.com Live Translate and multilingual-support articles).

The pieces are there — chat conversations overview with volume/performance/CSAT trend analysis, custom dashboards and an agent availability dashboard from Pro, and a Freddy AI Agent report carrying a ticket deflection rate. But independent reviewers keep landing on the same complaint, with Capterra's Suresh N. writing "no advanced reporting" and multiple reviewers noting analytics feel basic on lower tiers. Scored on what buyers report, not the feature list.

The seat pricing itself is clean and public: $0 up to 10 agents, then $19/$49/$79 per agent/month billed annually. What drags it down is everything stacked on top — Freddy AI Agent at $49/100 sessions, Copilot at $29/agent/month, plus day passes, campaign contact packs, and connector-task packs — and the absence of published monthly-billing rates, so the headline price is not the number most buyers will pay (freshworks.com/live-chat-software/pricing/).

Freshchat exposes a REST API v2 at an account-specific base URL covering conversations, messages, users, agents, groups, roles, and reports with bearer-token auth, plus webhook events (conversation created/resolved/reopened, message created, agent assigned, CSAT submitted) and the wider Freshworks app SDK and developer platform — you can genuinely build on top (developers.freshworks.com app-sdk REST APIs docs).

pricing.model: Per-agent tiered SaaS with usage-metered AI add-ons
pricing.startingPrice: $0 (free up to 10 agents); $19/agent/mo for the first paid tier

plans.notes: Web and mobile chat widget, shared inbox, email integration, roles and permissions. No social channels.

plans.name: Growth
plans.notes: Adds social messengers, SMS and WhatsApp, reporting, and access to Freddy AI Agent as a paid add-on ($49 per 100 sessions).

plans.name: Pro

plans.name: Freddy AI Agent (add-on)
plans.notes: 500 free sessions once per account on Growth, Pro, and Enterprise.

pricingBreakdown: Freshchat's headline is one of the most attractive in this category and one of the most misleading, and both facts matter. Attractive: $19/agent/month annual gets you WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS, LINE, and email in one inbox — Intercom's Essential tier is $29/seat/month for a narrower channel set, and Crisp's $45/month workspace bundles four seats but caps you there. A five-agent Freshchat team on Growth pays $95/month for more channels than either. The free plan is also unusually generous at up to 10 agents, where Crisp's free tier stops at 2. Misleading: none of the AI is in that number. Freddy AI Agent is $49 per 100 sessions after a one-time 500-session freebie, which means an honest comparison against Crisp (AI credits bundled into every paid tier) or Chatbase (message credits included in the plan) has to add a separate AI line to Freshchat's bill. At 1,000 automated conversations a month, that's $490 on top of seats — enough to flip Freshchat from the cheapest option to a mid-pack one. Add Copilot at $29/agent/month and a five-person team's real cost is $95 + $145 + AI sessions, not $95. Freshworks also doesn't publish monthly-billing rates for Freshchat, so if you won't commit to a year, budget above the sticker. My read: Freshchat is genuinely the value pick if humans are answering and channels are the problem. If AI deflection is the problem, price it out fully before you compare.

capabilities.note: This is the strongest thing about the product and the reason to shortlist it. Ten native channels — including WhatsApp Business, Instagram, Messenger, SMS, LINE, Apple Business Chat, and Google Business Messages — is more breadth per dollar than almost anything else at $19/agent. The asterisk is that social and SMS start at Growth, so the free plan is web-and-email only, and voice isn't here at all (that's Freshdesk Contact Center).

Consistently the best-reviewed part of Freshchat. Reviewers on both G2 and Capterra land on the same two words — clean and intuitive — and specifically credit having every channel in one interface. Private notes with @mentions, group and skill-based assignment rules, and shareable canned-response categories cover the team-collaboration basics properly rather than minimally.

Freddy AI Agent is technically capable — it grounds in your knowledge base, ingests URLs, and takes real actions against Shopify, Stripe, PayPal, and FedEx rather than just describing them. But it's an add-on billed per session, and that gap between 'available' and 'included' shows up in reviews: multiple Capterra reviewers describe Freshchat's AI as limited or missing, which is what happens when the AI is a purchase decision instead of a default. Judge the AI on a paid trial, not the base plan.

The weakest documented area relative to expectations. You get conversation volume, performance and CSAT trend reports, custom dashboards from Pro, and a Freddy deflection-rate report — but 'no advanced reporting' is a recurring reviewer complaint on Capterra, and the better dashboards are tier-gated. If reporting depth is a buying criterion, this is the thing to stress-test in the trial.

Better than the integrations page suggests. The REST API v2 covers conversations, messages, users, agents, groups, roles, and reports, webhooks fire on conversation and CSAT events, and there's a full app SDK and marketplace. The soft spot is no-code: Make.com has a Freshchat integration but Zapier's own community says there's no dedicated Freshchat Zapier app, so non-developers route through Freshdesk connectors or webhooks.

pros: Ten native channels including WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS, LINE, Apple Business Chat, and Google Business Messages — exceptional breadth for a $19/agent tier
Free plan supports up to 10 agents, far more headroom than the 2-seat free tiers common in this category
Inbox usability is the most consistently praised element across both G2 (~4.4/5, ~490 reviews) and Capterra (4.2/5, 151 reviews), with reviewers citing a clean interface and low learning curve
Genuine agentic AI actions are documented — order tracking, exchanges, inventory checks, subscription changes via Shopify, Stripe, PayPal, and FedEx — not just knowledge-base Q&A
Backed by a public company (Freshworks Inc., NASDAQ: FRSH, ~5,300 employees) with a real developer platform, REST API, webhooks, and marketplace
cons: AI is unbundled and usage-metered: $49 per 100 Freddy AI Agent sessions and $29/agent/month for Copilot on top of seat cost, which can quietly double a real bill
Reporting depth draws repeated criticism in independent reviews — Capterra reviewers use phrases like "no advanced reporting" and note AI features feel limited

Reliability and notifications are a recurring complaint theme, including a 1-star Capterra review from a founder describing a 13-day outage and lost conversations, and Trustpilot reviews about push notifications failing
Website-builder integrations are thin: official WordPress plugin aside, Wix, Squarespace, and Webflow are all manual code-injection, and there's no first-party WooCommerce or dedicated Zapier app
Voice isn't part of Freshchat — phone support means buying Freshdesk Contact Center or the Freshdesk Omni suite instead

sentiment.quote: One of its biggest strengths is how it brings conversations from multiple channels into a single interface, making it much easier for teams to manage and respond to chats efficiently.

Catastrophic. We centralized all customer communication for our e-commerce operation across 6 countries on Freshchat. When it went down for 13 days, we had no fallback. 6,500 conversations lost forever.
We lost many customers because the push notification doesn't work and the support won't help you.

bestFor: Support teams whose volume lives on WhatsApp, Instagram, and SMS and who want all of it natively at entry-tier pricing
Companies already running Freshdesk, Freshsales, or Freshservice, where Freshchat is the least-friction messaging layer to bolt on
Small teams that need more than two free seats before committing budget — the 10-agent free plan is a real runway
Buyers who want human agents in a clean shared inbox now and are content to add AI deflection later as a measured, separately-priced experiment
verdict: Freshchat is the channel-breadth pick, and I'd shortlist it on that alone. Ten native channels at $19 an agent, with a free plan that carries ten seats rather than two, is a better deal than Intercom or Crisp give you at the same tier — and the inbox itself is the part reviewers keep praising in almost identical words across G2 and Capterra: clean, fast to learn, everything in one view. What I'd push back on is the AI story. Freddy AI Agent is real and genuinely agentic on paper — Freshworks documents it tracking orders, processing exchanges, and hitting Shopify and Stripe — but it's sold at $49 per 100 sessions on top of seats, and that pricing decision shows up directly in the reviews, where Capterra users describe the AI as limited or "pretty much missing." Both things are true: the capability exists, and most Freshchat customers apparently aren't using it. Two honest caveats on my own confidence. Freshchat's 1.9/5 Trustpilot score rests on just 12 reviews and shouldn't be weighted heavily — but its themes (dead push notifications, unresponsive support) recur on Capterra too, including a founder's 1-star account of a 13-day outage, and that pattern is worth a hard look at your fallback plan. And I could not verify that Freshchat standalone includes Freddy sentiment analysis; every doc I found for it sits under Freshdesk. Buy it for channels and inbox. Budget the AI separately, and test it before you count on it.
